pr_title: Support view individual commit for wiki pages
pr_body: Currently you can see a list of commit history for wiki pages but aren't able to view the commit diff itself. This adds the feature to view an individual commit to a wiki repo. Closes #8999 Ultimately it might be nicer to have a different UI/flow for viewing the history of a wiki page that might make more sense for wiki pages but since we already use the commits list for revision history the actual content of the commit should be available too.

review_comments:
I would say that if the intention is that only commits are viewable here that this does not ensure this.

A good example is that I can create the branch `deadbeef` and this will be rendered as commit. (Passing a tree sha doesn't seem to work though - which is good.)

Hmm I just copied from the existing router for repos -- I suppose my only intention was that the link from the wiki history works.

I don't think it matters that you could manually type that in and see a commit since you would have permission to view it anyway, but would there be a simple way to prevent that?

I'm not certain there is a clean way tbh - even appending ^{commit} doesn't prevent git rev-parse parsing a reference.

The only solution is to rev-parse it and ensure that what comes back starts with what was put in?

(I recognized that they were a copy of those for the normal commits but I just thought I'd better alert people to this point.)
